hypothesis: A completed five-minute sweep of a causal one-hour structural high or low may predict enough next-open continuation or reclaim reversal to survive Hyperliquid fees, slippage, and funding with a candle-extreme structural stop, 2R target, and six-hour maximum hold.
decision: Reject both exact arms. Acceptance continuation and reclaim reversal were negative before fees, after nominal and stress friction, in every chronological fold, every BTC/SOL long/short cell, and every causal 15-minute regime slice. Do not tune nearby thresholds on the opened interval, train a model to rescue the negative base event, add either arm to v30, or increase leverage. Preserve live v25 while it owns positions; retain the fixed inactive v30 candidate at 1.00x for a separately authorized flat-boundary transition.
falsifier: The exact rejection is invalidated by changed evidence bytes, future input entering a decision row, structural history bridging an archive gap, signal-bar entry, incorrect barrier or stop-first ordering, overlapping lifecycles counted independently, or disproven fee/slippage/funding arithmetic. A materially different preregistered liquidity mechanism may update the broader research direction but would not falsify this exact contract.
limitations: Five-minute OHLC cannot recover sub-bar event order; simultaneous target and stop touches were resolved stop-first.
Terminal public L2 is not private IOC queue evidence; missing observed spread made a frozen structural barrier invalid rather than being silently filled.
Completed-bar fills cannot reproduce private acknowledgement latency or stop gaps.
